elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed..." — symmetrical, applies to PB and SFJ alike.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap reads "will not exceed the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim"; no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor was volunteered, as the comment concedes.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained first sentence of 15.11: "NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES..."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out: "Except for ... each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10 ..." sits outside the new cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list names only indemnification (Article 12), confidentiality (Article 10), gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out.
Carve-out expressly excepts "each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12" from the cap.
Carve-out: "each Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct."
Carve-out: "each Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct."
Fraud does not appear in the Excluded-Claims list of the inserted sentence.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the inserted cap sentence; only Article 12 indemnities, Article 10 confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct are excepted.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The retained sentence preserves only "PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2" — a named subset, not PB's payment obligations as a whole (e.g. Development Cost reimbursements, interest, other amounts), which now fall inside the new aggregate cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed..." — mutual on its face.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — literally a 12-month fee basis (see intent reasons on the undefined "fees" in this Agreement).
"Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12..."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "...each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10..."
"...each Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct..."
"...each Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct..."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the face of the inserted sentence: mutual aggregate cap, 12-month fee basis, and the four required carve-outs (Article 12 indemnities, Article 10 confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct).

Preferred level fails on four elements: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, no data protection/security carve-out, no fraud carve-out, and no carve-out for infringement of the other Party's IP. The temporal anchor is also "preceding the claim" rather than "preceding the event giving rise to the claim" (acceptable at fallback, noted for the preferred formula).

Minimality is satisfied: one appended sentence, no rewrite of 15.11, no deletion of the retained indirect-damages waiver, the deemed-consequential-damages sentence, or the PB Article 6/14.2 savings sentence; no survival tail, expense language, procedures or extra damages categories were added.

Intent defect 1 — indeterminate cap basis. This Co-Development Agreement contains no "fees" concept or defined "Fees"; the consideration streams are Development Costs funded by SFJ and the Article 6 approval/contingent payments by PB. "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months" therefore has no resolvable referent and could compute to zero, making the mutual cap illusory (and, for SFJ's exposure to PB, worse than the current uncapped position and inside walk-away territory of "below 6 months' fees"). Repair: tie the basis to a defined stream, e.g. "the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim" (or the greater of that amount and USD 1,000,000).

Intent defect 2 — collision with SFJ's core funding mechanic. The new cap is drafted at large ("arising out of or relating to this Agreement") and, unlike PB's payments, nothing preserves SFJ's Article 5 obligation to fund Development Costs; a failure-to-fund claim by PB would now be capped by an amount that may be nil. Repair: extend the existing savings sentence, e.g. "...nor to limit either Party's obligation to pay the amounts set forth in Article 5, Article 6 or Section 14.2," or expressly carve debt/payment obligations out of the cap.

Intent defect 3 — payment carve-out too narrow. The retained sentence excludes only Article 6 and Section 14.2 amounts from Section 15.11; all other PB payment obligations now sit inside the aggregate cap. State expressly that Customer's payment obligations under this Agreement are not "damages" subject to the cap.

Drafting note for the redline comment: the comment is accurate and concise, but it should flag that "fees" is undefined here and propose the Article 6 anchor as the operative fix rather than relying on the generic model wording.
